capabilities.summary: The host, not the RPC caller, decides whether a tournament candidate must be verified; protected paths and tamper policy are operator-owned.
One canonical, hashed intent covers every tournament field; a one-shot grant cannot be replayed or retargeted, and the revision and live token cap are re-checked after approval.
A workspace may lower but never raise the operator's token, concurrency and model-window ceilings; every clamp is reported, and a request that cannot fit the window is never sent.
limits: Without an operator-configured window the context check is a conservative report, not a hard refusal.

capabilities.summary: Each request reserves only a per-request output allowance, so retries and sibling children stay affordable; settlement is explicit (not dispatched / measured / estimated / unknown) and overage is audited.
Compaction identity lives in host-written typed metadata, not in tool text; a forged marker grants nothing and a stub says whether its raw bytes are still available.
Every untrusted read opens with O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK, verifies the type with fstat on the handle and streams at most limit+1 bytes; UTF-8 is validated after the size check.
limits: Windows has no O_NONBLOCK equivalent; the type check carries that case.

capabilities.summary: The writer checks the reader's line and file limits before the first byte, so a committed session is always resumable; disk-full and torn tails are handled transactionally.
limits: No segmented WAL or rotation: the format fails closed at 8 MiB per line / 64 MiB per file.

capabilities.summary: Windows takes a native exclusive byte-range lock (LockFileEx) on a lock file keyed by the normalised workspace path, so two processes cannot own the same workspace.
limits: Cross-process runtime cases are compiled for x86_64-pc-windows-gnu but NOT executed: no Windows runner is available in this environment (recorded BLOCKED in T08).

capabilities.summary: A per-run execution policy decides, per spawn class, whether the sandbox is required and whether the network is allowed; a required backend that is unavailable refuses the command instead of running it on the host.
limits: Only the agent's bash goes through the policy today; verifier/probe/hook spawns are not yet wired (T11 residual).
Default is host mode; isolation is opt-in via execution_sandbox = bwrap | container:<runtime>:<image>.

capabilities.summary: Containers are named and tracked by a cidfile in the trusted state area; cancellation stops, removes and verifies the workload, and a failed cleanup reports RecoveryRequired with the retained id.

live: real docker 26.1.5 with alpine:3.20 in tests/t10_container_lifecycle.rs

limits: Podman compatibility is not claimed: only a docker-compatible CLI was exercised.

capabilities.summary: One plan derived from the resolved configuration gives every surface the same budget, policy, execution boundary and feature eligibility; a mechanism whose dependency is missing fails at start.
limits: The RPC, worker and resume doors do not call RunPlan yet; equality is proven at the plan level, not at each door.
Mechanisms do not increment the executed counter in production, so a run reports 0 executions rather than a fabricated gain.

capabilities.summary: discover_tools can activate a schema for the next request (policy-checked, budgeted, ordered), so a provider that only permits declared tools can call what it discovered; unmount removes schema and dispatch.
limits: Activation is per run and not carried across --resume.

capabilities.summary: The client implements 2024-11-05 only: an unknown negotiated version is refused before notifications/initialized, tools/list is required to declare the capability, and the catalog is paginated with page/tool/schema/cursor bounds.
limits: stdio transport only; resources, prompts, sampling and remote transports are not claimed.
Server-to-client requests are not answered (they are not faked either).

capabilities.summary: The wire cache breakpoint follows the growing stable history instead of sitting at the frozen baseline, and cache writes are accounted separately from reads.
limits: No real-network cache canary has been run (NOT_RUN: needs budget and credentials).

capabilities.summary: Memory eviction is not deletion: evicted evidence is written to a keyed artifact (session/branch/event/hash) and reads verify the hash and directory privacy, reporting Available/Gone/Corrupt/Forbidden.
limits: 32 MiB per artifact; GC is explicit (by manifest reference), not scheduled.

capabilities.summary: A warm cache obeys the same file and byte budgets as a cold build, and the index carries comment words so a natural-language question can reach a file.
limits: Comment indexing is a heuristic scanner, not a parser.

capabilities.summary: A versioned manifest freezes arms, models, prices, sandbox, oracle, repeats and the holdout; duplicate ids, an empty or unknown holdout, an oversized matrix and an unknown field are all refused before any provider call.
limits: --experiment validates and dry-runs; manifest-driven provider bench execution is not wired (T24).

capabilities.summary: Every attempt is priced on the model it reported, cache writes and reads have distinct rates, and an estimate or missing usage makes the total explicitly incomplete instead of a number.
limits: Library-level: not yet consumed by the bench report or CLI output (T24).

capabilities.summary: The VCS probe is bounded and reports a timeout distinctly, the source hash reads through the bounded reader, unreadable input makes the identity incomplete, and the executable bit is part of it.
limits: The read-error branch is exercised through the size bound, because the test process runs as root.

capabilities.summary: The self-repair experimenter runs baseline and candidate from frozen copies, protects the judge (scorer, completion gate, AHE policy, trusted tests), splits prediction/validity/improvement/promotion, and never promotes by itself.
limits: Produces a candidate patch and a report only; promotion requires human approval after an independent regression.
